One repair.

Take the explanation with you.

Exports keep your controls, labels and source. GIF orbits ±30° around your current camera.

01 / THE RENDERER

These aren’t
just dots.

Each splat is a 3D ellipsoid with a position, covariance, opacity and color. Turn the camera: its projected ellipse changes, even though the 3D ellipsoid stays fixed.

Σ₂ᴅ = J R Σ₃ᴅ Rᵀ Jᵀ

R rotates world coordinates into the camera frame. J is the perspective projection’s Jacobian at the Gaussian center. Try the anisotropy slider with footprints on.

02 / THE IMAGE

Depth decides
who shows through.

This toy renderer sorts splats by camera-space center depth, then draws translucent Gaussian footprints from back to front. Overlapping opacity accumulates; it isn’t an average of the colors.

C = ∑ᵢ Tᵢ αᵢ cᵢ + Tᵦ cᵦ

Tᵢ = ∏ⱼ<ᵢ (1 − αⱼ), in front-to-back notation. Canvas uses the equivalent back-to-front source-over operation. Gradients approximate Gaussian falloff and are truncated at 3σ.

03 / THE NEW CONNECTION

Fill the scene,
then change the view.

WINGS (29 Sep 2026) studies inpainting directly in Gaussian scenes with a 3D generative prior, instead of using inpainted reference views. A shared 3D representation makes consistency a structural constraint.

The paper evaluates 29 scenes across three benchmarks. Reported results are the authors’ evaluation. Axis-alignment assumptions and missing higher-order spherical harmonics remain limitations; a public runnable release was not verified for this edition.

What this visual does—and doesn’t—show

The arch, mask and repair are hand-designed. The inconsistent repair is deliberately altered as the camera moves; it is not an output of any image model. The fixed repair is also handmade, not WINGS inference. Both panels use the same covariance projection and alpha-compositing renderer. This explains multiview consistency, not measured reconstruction quality, benchmark performance or learned appearance. A fixed 3D object can still be the wrong object.
